thread:
marta: quick sync — we need to align Python/TS/Go SDKs for paginated/streaming endpoints. current mismatch is causing user confusion and test flakes.
kevin: +1. what's the concrete divergence?
marta: python yields async iterator of items, TS returns async generator of pages (user has to flatten), Go exposes Paged calls with explicit PageToken. also retry semantics differ: python retries at call-level, TS retries at page-level.
oz: that's rough. Users expect consistent "iterate items" ergonomics across langs. I'd prefer: SDKs expose item-level async iterable as the primary ergonomic surface, and page-level helpers as opt-in.
samir: agree on ergonomics, but we need to consider transport cost: continuous streaming (gRPC stream) vs unary paging (HTTP1/2). Some backend routes are streaming-only for latency. How do we normalize without causing cross-proto hacks?
marta: proposal: define a small language-agnostic adapter layer in the client runtime that can normalize a page-stream or a raw item-stream into the same iterator interface. runtime provides two primitives: PaginatedCall and StreamedCall. both implement Iterable<Item>.
kevin: can you sketch the adapter shape?
marta: sure — pseudocode for Python adapter:
```
# adapter.py (concept)
class PaginatedAdapter:
    def __init__(self, page_call, retry_policy):
        self._page_call = page_call
        self._retry = retry_policy
    async def __aiter__(self):
        token = None
        while True:
            page = await self._retry.call(lambda: self._page_call(token))
            for item in page.items:
                yield item
            if not page.next_token:
                break
            token = page.next_token
```

and for TS: a similar lightweight wrapper that returns an AsyncIterable of items.

oz: looks good. central piece is the retry_policy abstraction. we should make retries composable (per-call, per-page, per-item). avoid surprising double-retries.
samir: exactly — opt for a single retry boundary: the adapter owns retry for page fetches; a streaming/grpc transport will own its own connection-level reconnection logic but must not auto-retry application-level idempotent work. document the invariants.
kevin: what about resume semantics for partial-page failures (e.g., timeout in the middle of streaming a page)? users expect at-least-once vs at-most-once guarantees.
marta: we need explicit recommendations:
- default: at-least-once items (simpler for clients, compatible with caching/duplicate suppression)
- provide idempotency tokens for callers to opt into at-most-once when backend supports stable resume tokens

samir: also call out telemetry: adapter should emit per-page token, retry count, latency. Console needs token-level cost breakdown.
devops-bot: deploy pipeline note: if we add adapter to runtime, mark it experimental and guard with feature flag for 2 weeks rollout.
kevin: practical SDK surface change:
- Python: expose IterItems() async iterator, keep existing list_pages for explicit page access (deprecated signal planned)
- TS: add items() helper on paginator that flattens pages (keeps pages API)
- Go: return an iterator type (Next() bool, Item() T, Err()) and keep paged helper.

oz: client ergonomics check — make examples tiny: one-liners developers can copy. Also ensure linters/types for TS work with AsyncIterable.
marta: follow-ups:
- API: add adapter shim in runtime repo (PR target: runtime/adapter)
- Docs: draft one-pager comparing server transports and adapter behaviors
- Telemetry: add events for page_fetch and stream_reconnect to Console schema
- Rollout: feature flag + canary on Dedicated then Hosted

kevin: any blockers? dependency on backend resume token support?
samir: yes for at-most-once. for at-least-once it's fine. backend teams need to confirm stream reconnection behavior.
marta: assigning tasks — @kevin to author runtime adapter PR, @samir to write the doc for transport invariants, @oz to update SDK examples. I'll open a GH issue to track.
kevin: I'll include tests: flaky-resume test harness that injects mid-page failures and verifies item ordering and dup handling.

oz: nits: add config knobs for max_pages_in_flight and prefetch window (affects batching). those live in Optimize later.

marta: thanks. created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/412 — please comment. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack, starting draft.
samir: will reach out to backend owners about resume semantics tomorrow.
